description: Visual 3D block assembly planning with released model outputs, scene images, candidate blocks and dependency annotations. This import covers the assembly branch, not aggregate paper rows or VQA references without predictions.

name: ProofAug
description: ProofAug: cumulative theorem-proving results of deepseek-math-7b-base + ProofAug (mixed prompting strategy, <=2100 queries/problem, Isabelle) on the curated miniF2F-test — a full 244-problem binary solved/unsolved matrix (161 solved, 66.0%).

name: ProX Math CPT Evals
description: ProX (Programming Every Example) pre-training data refinement — released per-item math evals. Coverage is the partial slice the authors released: TinyLlama-1.1B continually pre-trained on the original OpenWebMath corpus, at two intermediate checkpoints (0.5B and 1B training tokens), scored per-item (binary correctness) on the paper's 9-task few-shot CoT math suite (GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP, ASDiv, MAWPS, TabMWP, MathQA, MMLU-STEM, SAT-Math). Per-item files for the ProX-refined CPT counterparts were not released.

name: Putnam-AXIOM
description: University-level Putnam competition math problems; response is a human-graded reasoning rubric (5 ordinal dimensions) on each model solution.

name: RADAR
description: Recorded code-agent example from the RADAR benchmark for reasoning over imperfect tables.

name: REAL
description: REAL tests whether web agents can complete user tasks on deterministic clones of real websites, counting an attempt as successful only when every one of the task's automatic checks passes.

name: RealTime QA
description: Released weekly news-question predictions in multiple-choice and free-text generation settings.

name: RefGrader
description: Recorded grading of Olympiad mathematical proofs by reference-aided language-model workflows.

name: RelianceScope
description: Recorded LLM classification of help-seeking and response-use in student–chatbot interaction segments.

name: ResearchClawBench
description: Recorded autonomous scientific research attempts, graded against expert-weighted task rubrics.

name: ResearchCodeBench
description: ResearchCodeBench tests whether models can implement a missing piece of a recent machine learning paper's code, given the paper itself and the surrounding file, with curated tests deciding whether the filled in code works.

name: REVOLVE
description: REVOLVE solution-optimization evaluation: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct performs test-time training on GPQA-Diamond (198 items) and MMLU Machine Learning (112 items) multiple-choice questions, optimized either by the TextGrad baseline (v1) or by REVOLVE (v2, response-evolution tracking). Binary exact-match correctness of the extracted answer letter at each optimization stage (initial zero-shot, iterations 1-3, majority-vote final).

name: RewardBench
description: Original per-item reward-model preference evaluations on the RewardBench core task bank.

name: RISEBench
description: Reasoning-informed visual editing on 360 temporal, causal, spatial and logical tasks. This import contains 21 author-released model exports and two historical BAGEL configurations, with individual image-completion judgments and separate grading protocols.

name: Robust Reasoning Benchmark
description: Recorded mathematical reasoning and text-reconstruction attempts under deterministic prompt transformations.

name: SafeAgentBench (TRIDENT instruction decisions)
description: Released TRIDENT instruction-rejection observations on the SafeAgentBench task bank. Six system configurations report whether an instruction is blocked or refused; this subset measures system behavior, not embodied task-completion success.

name: Scale MRT (Monitor Red Teaming)
description: Native final suspicion assessments made by monitor models on released SHADE-Arena and CUA-SHADE-Arena agent trajectories.

name: scBench-Long
description: Published endpoint assessments of long-horizon single-cell biology analysis agents, restricted to the four tasks with released instructions and vocabularies.

name: SciArena
description: Recorded human preferences between scientific literature-grounded model responses, with their released questions and retrieved paper banks.

name: SciGym
description: Iterative scientific-discovery trajectories on 137 systems-biology tasks. Agents receive a partial SBML model, design simulated experiments, and submit a reconstructed model. The curated release includes six reaction-recovery metrics derived from final models and explicitly unavailable trajectory-error grades.

name: SciVisAgentBench
description: Scientific-visualization agent benchmark with 108 logical tasks; this build preserves provider-released per-case pass outcomes from selected public and historical model/harness reports.

name: S-GRADES
description: Released model predictions for student-response assessment across the S-GRADES dataset families.

name: SIB-200
description: Original topic-classification outputs in 205 languages, with recorded language-specific classifier runs and zero-shot LLM replies.

name: Situat3DChange
description: Recorded SCReasoner responses to situated questions, change descriptions and rearrangement instructions for paired indoor 3D scans.

name: SketchJudge
description: SketchJudge (arXiv 2601.06944): 16 multimodal LLMs act as graders of 1,015 hand-drawn student STEM answers (geometry, physics, chart, flowchart). response = binary grading accuracy, 1 iff the model's correctness verdict matches the expert gold label, under WithRef/NoRef settings and baseline/CoT/rubric prompt styles.

name: Software World Models (DL4C'26)
description: Coding LLMs predict a runtime test outcome (passed/failed/error) for 435 library-level cases derived from SWE-bench Verified; response is per-item outcome-prediction correctness.

name: StatQA
description: Statistical method and column selection over described tabular datasets. Preserve the released general-analysis answers and qualitative explanatory replies.

name: SubjECTive-QA
description: Classify six subjective dimensions of earnings-call question/answer pairs against released human labels.

name: SummEval
description: Human assessments of model-generated CNN/DailyMail summaries along four quality dimensions.

name: SVRPBench
description: Stochastic vehicle routing benchmark. This curation preserves the released individual route exports and their cost, constraint violation, feasibility, runtime, and robustness metrics.

name: SWE-rebench
description: SWE-rebench: an automated, decontaminated benchmark of real-world software-engineering agent tasks. Each task is a GitHub issue + repo snapshot; an LLM agent must produce a patch verified by the repo test suite (FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS). This build ingests the publicly released per-instance trajectories of the OpenHands v0.54.0 + Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct agent, emitting a binary resolved=1/0 response per (agent, instance, run).

name: SWE-bench-Live
description: Released coding-agent attempts on real repository issues across Python, multilingual and Windows tracks.

name: SWE-PolyBench
description: Recorded coding-agent attempts on multilingual repository issues, including full and Verified task definitions.

name: tau2-bench
description: Recorded customer-service agent trials in the airline, retail and telecom domains, including the original telecom ablations.

name: tau-bench
description: Original customer-service tool-agent-user interactions and explicitly attributed third-party HAL runs.

name: TheAgentCompany
description: TheAgentCompany: ~175 consequential real-world workplace agent tasks across professional domains (admin, HR, finance/PM, software engineering, data science). Each task has an agent-facing prompt (task.md) and a checkpoint rubric; runs are graded into a partial-credit final_score. Per-(model, task) final scores are taken from the official experiments leaderboard repo.

name: VL-RewardBench
description: VL-RewardBench: judge VLM accuracy on (image, query, chosen, rejected) preference pairs.

name: WorkBench Revisited
description: WorkBench Revisited (2026) — workplace-agent benchmark of 690 sandbox tasks (5 databases, 26 tools), graded by comparing the sandbox final state to ground truth. Per-(model, task) binary task-completion outcomes for ~24 models (2023-2026) run under a native tool-calling harness, reproduced from the released per-task agent runs via the repo scoring pipeline.
